newsitem.title: USA: NY county eyes investigation of heating oil prices.
newsitem.headline: NY county eyes investigation of heating oil prices.

text.p: A New York county official said Thursday he requested a state investigation of home heating oil prices to ensure the community protection against price gouging.

Westchester County executive Andrew P. O'Rourke said he requested the investigation after a county Department of Consumer Protection survey on Dec. 18 showed that home heating oil prices cost 18 percent more than last year.

"Certainly, a variety of legitimate market forces may have combined to raise prices (in Westchester) to some degree this time of year," said O'Rourke. "However, I want to make sure that no one is taking advantage of that situation to manipulate prices out of greed."
O'Rourke said that any indications of price gouging should be met with swift action and maximum penalties.
"Home heating oil is not a luxury. For many people with low or fixed incomes, price gouging can be a threat to health and safety," O'Rourke added.
U.S. heating oil prices have shot up more than 50 percent from lows this year to a post-Gulf War high in October largely due to worries of shortages in the large East Coast market.
Prices since October, which reached 76.75 cents, have come down some because of high output, but prices are still well above last year.
